summary: Each flake's thickness comes from the A1g−E2g separation Δ, the standard MoS2 layer-number indicator (Lee et al. 2010). Measured Δ: A 21.46, B 19.23, C 25.06, D 24.27 cm-1. Read against the Lee et al. trend: B is about 1–2 layers, A about 3–4 layers, and C and D are thick and bulk-like (at least about 5 layers). Δ alone cannot separate 1 L from 2 L or 5 L from bulk, and the layer numbers are approximate because I could not verify the numeric Δ thresholds against the full paper text. Ranking the flakes thin to thick: B < A < D ≈ C. C and D cannot be ranked against each other with confidence.

observations.finding: All four spectra show the 2H-MoS2 E2g/A1g pair plus the Si 520 cm-1 substrate line, with no unexplained strong bands in 360–540 cm-1.
observations.evidence: Pseudo-Voigt fits (360–540 cm-1, quadratic baseline): A E2g 383.37, A1g 404.82, Si 520.02; B 383.91, 403.13, 520.00; C 382.24, 407.31, 519.95; D 382.37, 406.64, 519.99 cm-1. Fit residual RMS ≈ per-point noise (15–22 counts) in every window, so no unmodelled structure is visible.

observations.finding: Δ = A1g − E2g separates the flakes into three groups: B (19.2) is the thinnest, A (21.5) is intermediate, and C (25.1) and D (24.3) are the thickest.
observations.evidence: Δ_A = 21.46, Δ_B = 19.23, Δ_C = 25.06, Δ_D = 24.27 cm-1. Changing the fit window (340–540, 350–460, 360–440, 370–425 cm-1) or the baseline order (1–3) moves Δ by at most 0.03 cm-1. Fit statistical errors on the centres are ≤0.1 cm-1 for the strong peaks (0.3 cm-1 for the weak Si in C), so the B–A and A–C gaps are far larger than the fit error. The C–D difference (0.8 cm-1) is not robust to the systematics listed under caveats.

observations.finding: Layer estimates from Δ: B ≈ 1–2 layers (Δ at the monolayer/bilayer edge), A ≈ 3–4 layers, C and D bulk-like (at least about 5 layers, not resolvable further).
observations.evidence: Δ thresholds: monolayer about 18–19 cm-1, bulk about 25 cm-1, intermediate values for few layers, from Lee et al. 2010 at 514.5 nm (values recalled from the paper, not verified in its full text). The same paper's abstract confirms the direction: the E2g frequency decreases and the A1g frequency increases with thickness.

observations.finding: Calibrated (Si-corrected) positions move the same way as thickness in the Lee et al. trend: E2g softens and A1g hardens from B to C.
observations.evidence: Si correction (520.7 − measured Si) = +0.68 (A), +0.70 (B), +0.75 (C), +0.71 (D) cm-1. Corrected E2g: A 384.05, B 384.61, D 383.08, C 382.99. Corrected A1g: B 403.83, A 405.50, D 407.35, C 408.06 cm-1. The ordering is monotonic in Δ. This agrees qualitatively with the Lee et al. abstract, and the B values sit near the monolayer-like absolute positions and C/D near bulk-like ones.

observations.finding: The absolute E2g/A1g intensities are not comparable between flakes; they do not indicate thickness.
observations.evidence: E2g peak heights: A 1269, B 666, C 335, D 2581 counts; A1g: 416, 277, 239, 1202. These values depend on focus, integration, laser power and flake/substrate interference, none of which are given for each flake.

observations.finding: Qualitative cross-check: the Si-520 line relative to the E2g line falls with thickness, consistent with attenuation of the substrate signal by the flake. Treat as weak evidence only.
observations.evidence: Si/E2g height ratio: B 2.5, A 1.0, D 0.36, C 0.2 (from fitted heights; Si in C is only 68 counts, with a fit error of 0.3 cm-1 on its position). The ratio also depends on spot position on each flake and on focus.

observations.finding: E2g is sharp in all four flakes; the A1g width varies more than the E2g width.
observations.evidence: Fitted FWHM: E2g 2.06–2.21 cm-1 in all four; A1g FWHM A 6.6, B 5.0, D 4.6, C 3.1 cm-1, stable across fit windows. The E2g FWHM is below the stated 2.7 cm-1 resolution, which is inconsistent with the instrument resolution as stated.

observations.finding: Weak bands near 228, 287 and 452 cm-1 (LA(M), E1g, 2LA(M)) are not robustly detected; I make no claim from them.
observations.evidence: Fitted heights are 2–43 counts against per-point noise of 12–22 counts, and the fitted widths and centres are unstable (e.g. 2LA(M) at 449.9 in C vs 452.6–453.2 in others; E1g FWHM 1–16 cm-1). Raman spectra range from 150 to 650 cm-1 only.

observations.finding: One cosmic-ray artifact in C was removed; no other single-point spikes affect the peaks.
observations.evidence: C at 265.09 cm-1: 3317 counts against 340–360 neighbours, a single point. Interpolated from its two neighbours before fitting. Other single-point bumps (B at 213.27, D at 202.37, about 80 counts above neighbours) are within a few sigma of noise and were left in.

properties.name: layers
properties.value: B: 1–2; A: ~3–4; C: bulk-like (≳5, not resolved); D: bulk-like (≳5, not resolved)
properties.source: [doi:10.1021/nn1003937](https://doi.org/10.1021/nn1003937) (Lee et al. 2010; Δ thresholds recalled, not verified in full text)

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: not assessed quantitatively; E2g width is sharp (≈2.1 cm-1); A1g width varies (3–6.6 cm-1) without a demonstrated cause

caveats: Δ thresholds per layer number are from my recollection of Lee et al. 2010 (about 18–19 cm-1 monolayer, about 25 cm-1 bulk); the paper's abstract confirms the trend, not the numbers. Verify the calibration against Fig. 2/3 of the full text before publishing layer numbers.

Δ is not purely thickness: strain, doping (electron doping softens A1g in the literature), laser heating and substrate can shift the two modes by fractions to about 1 cm-1 each. Such shifts could move B relative to A across the monolayer/bilayer boundary. Not quantified here.

The Si reference (520.7 cm-1 at room temperature) is from memory, not checked against a reference. A rigid Si offset cancels in Δ but changes the absolute positions used for the calibrated-frame comparison.

Absolute positions in the corrected frame assume the spectrometer offset is the same for all four; the Si scatter (519.95–520.02 cm-1) suggests that is reasonable, but the Si line in C is weak (±0.3 cm-1).

The stated resolution (2.7 cm-1) is inconsistent with the fitted E2g FWHM (≈2.1 cm-1). Either the resolution is overstated, or the pseudo-Voigt fits underestimate widths. Peak positions are unaffected at the level discussed, but the linewidth comparisons are not reliable in absolute terms.

The 514.5 nm laser energy (2.41 eV) is off the A and B excitons, so resonance should not dominate; but Δ and intensities can depend on excitation energy, so the thresholds should only be applied at a similar wavelength (Lee et al. used 514.5 nm).
Cosmic-ray removal in C affects only the point at 265.09 cm-1.
Lateral position on each flake, laser power, integration time and whether each flake was measured at the same spot are unknown; intensity comparisons are not meaningful without these.
questions_for_user: Is this natural molybdenite 2H, or could some flakes be 3R? A 3R stacking would change the low-frequency and E-mode assignments and the Δ thresholds.
What laser power at the sample, integration time, and spot size did you use? Were the four spectra taken at identical conditions? Absolute intensities cannot be compared without this.

Can you measure below 150 cm-1 (about 10–50 cm-1)? The shear and layer-breathing modes are the most direct layer-number probes; the references are [doi:10.1063/1.4751266](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4751266), [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.86.241301](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.86.241301), [doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.87.115413](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.87.115413). Your spectra start at 150 cm-1, so these are missing.
Do you have a reference Si spectrum taken on the same instrument to set the absolute calibration? This affects the absolute positions, not Δ.

Can you get a photoluminescence map or an AFM height profile? PL distinguishes monolayer from few-layer (direct-gap A exciton); AFM gives step heights and would settle the 1–2 L and 3–4 L assignments and the C vs D question.
Is the 285 nm SiO2 thickness accurate to a few nm? Optical contrast on Si/SiO2 is the usual layer check, and it would help confirm which flake is monolayer.
citations: [doi:10.1021/nn1003937](https://doi.org/10.1021/nn1003937) — Lee, C. et al., ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010); arXiv [1005.2509](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.2509). Source of the A1g/E2g thickness trend (confirmed from abstract); Δ numerical thresholds recalled, not verified in full text.

[doi:10.1063/1.4751266](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4751266) — Plechinger, G. et al. (2012), shear mode in few-layer MoS2. Low-frequency reference; not measurable in this data (range starts at 150 cm-1).
[doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.86.241301](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.86.241301) — Zeng, H. et al., PRB 86, 241301 (2012); low-frequency shear and compression modes in MoS2. Not measurable in this data.

[doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.87.115413](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.87.115413) — Zhang, X. et al., PRB 87, 115413 (2013); shear and layer-breathing modes in multilayer MoS2. Not measurable in this data.

[doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.88.075320](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.88.075320) — Luo, X. et al., PRB 88, 075320 (2013); surface effects on E2g/A1g frequencies in thin MoS2, a possible alternative explanation for the E2g trend.
limits: Layer numbers are approximate. Δ alone cannot distinguish 1 L from 2 L, or 5 L from bulk, and the numerical thresholds are unverified recollections of Lee et al. 2010.

I did not use the ramanlens skill's scripts or reference notes: they live outside this working folder, which the instructions restrict me from reading. The analysis used numpy/scipy only, with my own fitting code in this folder (mos2_fit.py, mos2_full.py, mos2_sens.py, fit_summary_window360_540.json).
The Si reference value 520.7 cm-1 and the bulk/monolayer absolute positions (≈383/408 and ≈385/404 cm-1) are recalled from the literature, not verified here.
No AFM, PL or low-frequency Raman data, so I cannot confirm any layer number independently. Strain, doping, heating and defect contributions to Δ were not quantified.
I did not verify the Lee et al. figure values or the rejected hypotheses (strain, doping, heating, substrate) numerically; they remain alternatives.
